name: Ayere
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Lawal, A.A. 1982. Phonology of the Ayere language. University of Ilorin MA thesis.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ayere language' (accessed 2026-09-17); Glottolog 5.x languoid page ayer1245
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; used only to locate Blench 2007 URL, the ELAR deposit and PHOIBLE link.

sources.citation: Choon, Anja (SOAS). Uwu documentation corpus and any accompanying phonological sketch / MA dissertation from the 2007-2010 ELDP-funded project (ELAR dk0231).
sources.note: The depositor recorded and analysed the language for three years; the deposit description already gives the tone system; any write-up (SOAS dissertation or field notes bundle) would be the modern primary description. Deposit content requires an ELAR account.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Ayere and Ahan languages of Central Nigeria and their affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 5 Feb 2007. Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 27 pp. (Glottolog ref 28099)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 1-2) gives only a 7-vowel chart and a consonant chart; the heading 3.3 'Tones' has no text under it; secs 2, 4, 5 are likewise empty. The Olumorin 1961 wordlist (pp. 3-24) carries partial tone marks (ígwú, adòdó, uyɛ́, iwɔ́wɔ́). a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing. downloaded via the Internet Archive (rogerblench.info blocks automated download with a captcha); 2015 and 2025 captures byte-identical.

sources.citation: Choon, Anja (depositor). 2007-2010. Documentation of Uwu, an endangered and undocumented minority language of the Nigerian Middle Belt. ELAR deposit dk0231 (formerly elar.soas.ac.uk/deposit/0231), SOAS.
sources.note: Deposit description (read via direct download; Preservica JS challenge blocks a raw save) states: 'Ayere has three level tones (and maybe glide tones and grammatical tones as well)', (V)CV syllables, syllabic nasal n/ŋ/m, Yoruba-like vowel harmony. No mention of stress or accent; no phonology write-up listed among the materials; cites Olumorin 1961, Blench 2006, Capo 1989.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010. The Uwu and Aha languages of Central Nigeria and their affinities. Unpublished ms. (PHOIBLE source 1545_uwu_ahan, file)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Later draft of the 2007 paper with the phonology filled in (PHOIBLE extracted a 43-segment inventory and three tones from it); the most likely place for any prose on tone vs. stress. Not posted on rogerblench.info (the Internet Archive's index has no Uwu file); would need to come from the author or from PHOIBLE's GM contributors.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1989. Defoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo languages, 275-290. Lanham: University Press of America.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Overview chapter that places Ayere in Defoid and gives comparative phonological notes on tone in the group; cited by the ELAR deposit. Unlikely to address stress but is the standard secondary reference.

sources.citation: Bamigboye, G. A. 1987. A study of the noun phrase of Ayere. MA thesis, University of Ilorin.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only other descriptive thesis on Ayere; a syntax thesis, but Ilorin MA theses usually open with a phonological sketch that could carry a tone/stress remark.

sources.citation: Lawal, A. A. 1982. Phonology of the Ayere language. MA thesis, University of Ilorin.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only dedicated phonology of Ayere; the source the earlier scan named; a Nigerian MA phonology would normally have a suprasegmentals chapter (tone, possibly a remark on stress).

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory GM 1545 'Uwu' (Green & Moran), source: Blench, Roger. 2010. The Uwu and Aha languages of Central Nigeria and their affinities. Unpublished ms.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
